Tell me which file exists (`ls /etc/pam.d | grep -E 'sshd|ssh'`), and I’ll give you the exact line/placement.  

In general, to run a script on *every login attempt* (success or failure), add this near the top of the SSH PAM file (before any `auth` includes), e.g.:

```pam
auth  optional  pam_exec.so  expose_authtok  /path/to/your-script.sh
```

- Put it under the **`auth`** section to trigger on authentication attempts.
- Use an absolute path, ensure the script is root-owned and executable.

arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Log PAM environment + any stdin (e.g., password if expose_authtok is used).
# WARNING: If pam_exec is configured with expose_authtok, stdin may contain secrets.
# Restrict permissions and avoid using expose_authtok unless you really mean it.

set -eu

LOG_DIR="/var/log/pam-exec"
TS="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
PID="$$"

umask 077
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

OUT="$LOG_DIR/login-${TS}-${PID}.log"

{
  echo "timestamp_utc=$TS"
  echo "pid=$PID"
  echo "argv=$0 $*"
  echo "--- env ---"
  env | sort
  echo "--- stdin (hex + text) ---"
  # Read up to 4096 bytes from stdin to avoid blocking/huge logs.
  # Save a hex dump plus a sanitized text view.
  IN_RAW="$LOG_DIR/login-${TS}-${PID}.stdin"
  dd bs=1 count=4096 of="$IN_RAW" 2>/dev/null || true
  echo "stdin_bytes=$(wc -c < "$IN_RAW" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  echo "stdin_path=$IN_RAW"
  echo "-- hex --"
  if command -v xxd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    xxd -g 1 "$IN_RAW" || true
  else
    od -An -tx1 -v "$IN_RAW" || true
  fi
  echo "-- text (nonprintables replaced) --"
  LC_ALL=C tr -c '[:print:]\n\t' '.' < "$IN_RAW" || true
} >"$OUT" 2>&1

exit 0
